question_text: Find the number of ways of selecting 7 members from a contingent of 10 soldiers.

recall_prompt: Say how you would count the selections of seven soldiers from ten — why it is a combination, and the number.
insider_note: A selection has no order, so the answer is ¹⁰C₇ — and the short route is the complement, ¹⁰C₇ = ¹⁰C₃ = 120: three factors over 3! instead of seven.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: A selection, so ¹⁰C₇
steps.margin_note: First mark. Members are selected, not arranged, so ¹⁰C₇; and ¹⁰C₇ = ¹⁰C₃ shortens the arithmetic.
lines: Selecting 7 members: order does not matter.

recall.must_convey: That selecting 7 of 10 is the combination 10 C 7, which equals 10 C 3.
accept: selection so ten C seven which is ten C three
order does not matter, ten C seven
ten C seven equals ten C three by the complement rule
select cheyadam kabatti ten C seven, adi ten C three
a combination of ten taken seven

steps.why: Selecting 7 to include is the same as selecting 3 to leave out, which is why ¹⁰C₇ = ¹⁰C₃ and three factors suffice instead of seven.
common_mistakes: Using ¹⁰P₇ = 604800 — the members are not ordered.

steps.label: Evaluate ¹⁰C₃

recall.must_convey: That 10 C 3 is 10 times 9 times 8 over 6 = 120.
accept: ten into nine into eight by six is one twenty
seven twenty by six is one twenty
the answer is one hundred and twenty ways

steps.why: Three factors over 3! give 120; the value is the answer.
common_mistakes: Computing 10·9·8 = 720 and forgetting to divide by 6.
